H1.text: A dark kitchen at night. A light flicks on. A cockroach dashes under the shelf.

H2.text: Gone in a second, before anyone could move.

H3.text: Aarav saw it happen. He asked: how did it sense him so fast? And how does a body with no bones keep its shape?

H4.text: Two features answer that. A hard outer skeleton made of chitin. And sense organs and nerves spread all along its body.

H5.text: By the end, you will know the cockroach's body, mouth parts and wings, and its digestion, blood, breathing, excretion, nerves and life cycle.

B1.text: First, meet the cockroach, Periplaneta americana.

B2.text: It is brown or black, about 34 to 53 millimetres long. It is active at night, eats almost anything, and lives in damp places.

B3.text: Its body has three parts: head, thorax and abdomen. A hard exoskeleton of chitin covers it, made of plates called sclerites, joined by thin, bendy arthrodial membranes.

Z2.text: The thorax has three parts: prothorax, mesothorax and metathorax. Each one bears a pair of walking legs.

Z3.text: Zoom to the head. It is triangular, made of six fused segments, with a pair of compound eyes and two long, thread-like antennae that sense the surroundings.

Z4.text: Now the mouth parts, made for biting and chewing. An upper lip, the labrum. A pair of mandibles and a pair of maxillae. And a lower lip, the labium.

Z5.text: In the middle sits the hypopharynx, which works like a tongue.

L1.text: Now its wings and abdomen, step by step.

L2.text: Step one. The first pair of wings grows from the mesothorax. These forewings are the tegmina: dark, leathery and opaque. They cover the hind wings at rest.

L3.text: Step two. The second pair grows from the metathorax. These hind wings are thin, see-through, and used for flying.

L4.text: Step three. The abdomen has ten segments, in both males and females.

L5.text: Step four. In females, the seventh, eighth and ninth sterna, the plates on the belly side, form a brood pouch, the genital pouch.

L6.text: Step five. Both sexes have a pair of jointed anal cerci on the tenth segment. Only males have short, thread-like anal styles.

T1.text: Remember this. Forewings are tegmina. Hind wings fly.

C1.text: Now inside. Follow food through the cockroach.

C2.text: From the mouth, food passes the pharynx and oesophagus into the crop, a sac that stores food.

C3.text: Next is the gizzard. Inside it are six hard, chitinous plates, called teeth, that grind the food.

C4.text: Where the foregut meets the midgut, six to eight hepatic caeca make digestive juice. Where the midgut meets the hindgut, thin Malpighian tubules join the gut.

D1.text: A cockroach breathes and moves its blood very differently from us.

D2.text: It breathes through a network of tubes called tracheae. They open outside through ten pairs of small holes, the spiracles, on the sides of the body. Air travels straight to the cells.

D3.text: Its blood system is open. The few blood vessels open into a space, the haemocoel. The blood, called haemolymph, is colourless.

D4.text: A long, tube-shaped heart runs along the back. Its chambers have tiny openings, the ostia, on each side.

U1.text: Waste is removed by the Malpighian tubules. The cockroach excretes uric acid, so it is uricotelic.

U2.text: Its nervous system is a chain of ganglia, small knots of nerve cells, along the belly side. Three are in the thorax and six in the abdomen. In the head, the brain is the supra-oesophageal ganglion.

U3.text: Because nerves run all along the body, a headless cockroach can live for up to a week. And each compound eye has about two thousand units, the ommatidia, giving mosaic vision.

U4.text: Your turn. Which removes waste from a cockroach's blood: the gizzard, or the Malpighian tubules? Pause and decide.

U5.text: The Malpighian tubules! The gizzard only grinds food.

W1.text: Now, a worked example. The life of a cockroach, from egg to adult.

W2.text: The sexes are separate. Males have a pair of testes. Females have a pair of large ovaries, each made of eight ovarioles.

W3.text: Fertilised eggs are packed in a dark brown capsule, the ootheca. A female makes nine to ten oothecae, each with fourteen to sixteen eggs.

W4.text: A nymph hatches. It looks like a small adult without wings, and it moults about thirteen times.

W5.text: Only the adult has wings. Growing through nymphs like this is called paurometabolous development.

X2.text: Many students think a cockroach's blood flows in closed tubes, like ours.

X3.text: But its system is open. Haemolymph flows into the haemocoel and bathes the organs directly.

E1.text: Where is this asked? As statement or match questions on mouth parts, wings, Malpighian tubules and the ootheca.

Q1.text: Exam level now. Match each part with its job. Pause and solve.

A1.text: The answer is A. One-q, two-p, three-s, four-r.

A2.text: Tegmina are the forewings. The gizzard grinds food.

A3.text: Malpighian tubules remove waste. And the ootheca is the egg capsule.

Y2.text: One. How many pairs of spiracles does a cockroach have?

Y3.text: Two. What does the gizzard do?

N1.text: Next time: a frog, a cockroach and you are all built from tiny living units. What are they? We find out in cell, the unit of life.
